newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EURO COMPETITIONS WADE THOUGH PRELIMINARIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EURO COMPETITIONS WADE THOUGH PRELIMINARIES.

text.p: Europe's ever-burgeoning club soccer competitions continue this week with an extensive line-up of preliminary round fixtures over three days.
Sixteen matches are played in the European Cup on Wednesday with the winners advancing to the expanded Champions' League and the losers claiming a consolation prize of a place in the UEFA Cup.
That competition is at its second preliminary round stage while the Cup Winners' Cup swings into action with 15 qualifying round ties which read like a Who's Who of the "Soccer Minnows Society".

To complete the line-up there are three "finals" of the Intertoto Cup, with the winners advancing to the UEFA Cup. France has four teams in those finals and three victories would give them an unprecedented 10 teams in Europe this season. With two facing each other they are already guaranteed eight.

The pick of them, champions Paris St Germain, have been one of the continent's most successful sides in recent years, reaching five successive European semifinals and winning the Cup Winners' Cup in 1986.
This year they are in the European Cup and face an awkward tie against former winners Steaua Bucharest.
The Romanians, champions in 1986, have begun their season with three wins and have home advantage on Wednesday.

Parma, another consistent recent performer, get their first run in Europe's premier competition despite never having won the Italian League. Included as a runner-up, they travel to Poland to play Widzew Lodz.
"We already have Champions' League experience and are not afraid of Parma," said striker Jacek Dembinski.
Glasgow Rangers, champions of Scotland for nine years in a row but seemingly out of their depth in Europe, face a difficult fixture against IFK Gothenburg.
Other big names in action include Barcelona, who play Latvia's Skonto Riga, Feyenoord, who face Finland's Jazz Pori and Newcastle, who take on Croatia Zagreb.
The UEFA Cup continues to whittle itself down to manageable proportions with its second preliminary round on Tuesday.
Scotland's Dundee United rattled up a 17-0 aggregate against Andorran side CE Pricipat two weeks ago but might find things a bit tougher against Trabzonspor of Turkey.

The Turkish fans have been known to besiege the opposing team's hotel, singing and banging drums all night before a big match, but home coach Yilmaz Vural was not complaining: "We are expecting the fans to be behind us all the way," he said. "We'll use all the weapons we have."
Fellow Scots Celtic travel to Austria's Tirol Innsbruck, who are without suspended defender Michael Streiter.
Two Swedish UEFA Cup contenders met in the league on Sunday with Malmo thrashing Orebro 5-0. Malmo travel to Croatia to meet Hadjuk Split while Orebro are away to Czech side Jablonec.
The Cup Winners' Cup qualifying round takes place on Thursday with the representatives of Europe's smaller footballing nations in action.
But alongside the teams from Armenia, Liechtenstein, Azerbaijan, Estonia and the Faroe Islands are some from countries rich in soccer heritage.

Yugoslavia's Red Star Belgrade, European Champions in 1991, play HJK Helsinki, Scotland is represented by Kilmarnock in an all-Celtic clash with Ireland's Shelbourne and Romania's National Bucharest travel to the unlikely surroundings of Welsh part-timers Cwmbran Town.
The Intertoto finals feature Montpellier v Lyon in the all-French clash, Halmstad of Sweden against Bastia of France and Germany's Duisburg against 1996 French double winners Auxerre.
